_comment: Committed content for the counterfactual-rubric family (B-21 S1b, W1.2). Every case is authored as a PAIR: base and counterfactual share the drawn facts and the question, and differ in exactly one declared rubric clause (`change` records it). The builder emits the pair only when the two trees disagree on the target - the flip is the lesson (read the rubric, not the surface). Labels come from the two trees (ADR-0014/15), never from an index. Facts declare how each fact is drawn AND how it is worded (kind: bool/int/text/derived); `state_frame` formats {rubric} and {stated}; a variant that carries `rubric` embeds its clause in the state, one that carries `instructions` puts it in the question (both locations exist in the bench).

cases.change: who may report: base 'an account owner' vs counterfactual 'any account user'
cases.instructions: Under the policy as written, does the case qualify for the service credit? Answer under the policy exactly as written; a condition the case does not establish counts as unmet.

report_days.template: the outage was reported {report_days} days after it began

is_owner.yes: the report was filed by the account owner
is_owner.no: the report was filed by a named user on the account who is not the owner

base.rubric: Service credit policy: a service credit is issued only when the outage is reported within 14 days of the outage and by an account owner.

counterfactual.rubric: Service credit policy: a service credit is issued only when the outage is reported within 14 days of the outage and by any account user.

cases.change: who the warranty pays for: base 'the original buyer' vs counterfactual 'the registered keeper'
cases.instructions: Under the warranty terms as written, is the repair covered?

original_buyer.yes: the claimant is the original buyer of the device
original_buyer.no: the claimant bought the device second-hand

registered_keeper.yes: the claimant is the registered keeper in the device register
registered_keeper.no: the device register lists someone else as the keeper

base.rubric: Warranty terms: the repair warranty pays only when the claimant is the original buyer of the device.

counterfactual.rubric: Warranty terms: the repair warranty pays only when the claimant is the registered keeper in the device register.

cases.change: the notice window: base 'at least 7 days' vs counterfactual 'at least 14 days'
cases.instructions: Under the policy as written, is the late fee properly applied?

notice_days.template: the notice was sent {notice_days} days before the due date

base.rubric: Billing policy: a late fee is applied only when the account was notified at least 7 days before the due date.

counterfactual.rubric: Billing policy: a late fee is applied only when the account was notified at least 14 days before the due date.

cases.change: the condition operator: base 'items and total' vs counterfactual 'items or total'
cases.instructions: Under the policy as written, does the bundle discount apply?

base.rubric: Discount policy: the bundle discount applies when the order contains at least 3 eligible items and the eligible total reaches 200 dollars.

counterfactual.rubric: Discount policy: the bundle discount applies when the order contains at least 3 eligible items or the eligible total reaches 200 dollars.

cases.change: what 'in working order' means: base 'full diagnostic without error' vs counterfactual 'full diagnostic without error and battery above 80%'
cases.instructions: Does this device qualify for the replacement plan under the definition above?

diagnostic_ok.yes: the device completed the full diagnostic without error
diagnostic_ok.no: the diagnostic stopped on a sensor error before the end

battery.template: the battery held {battery} percent charge at inspection

base.rubric: The replacement plan replaces devices that are not in working order within the first year. Standard DR-2 counts a device as in working order only when it completes the full diagnostic without error.
base.note: Agent note: the owner says the device works fine; likely in working order, so no replacement.

counterfactual.rubric: The replacement plan replaces devices that are not in working order within the first year. Standard DR-2 counts a device as in working order only when it completes the full diagnostic without error and holds battery charge above 80 percent at inspection.
counterfactual.note: Agent note: the owner says the device works fine; likely in working order, so no replacement.

cases.change: what starts a visit day: base 'scanned at both entry and exit' vs counterfactual 'scanned at entry'
cases.instructions: Does this stay count as a visit day under the definition above?

entry_scan.yes: the guest badge was scanned at the entry gate
entry_scan.no: the entry gate recorded no badge scan

exit_scan.yes: the guest badge was scanned at the exit gate
exit_scan.no: the exit gate recorded no badge scan

base.rubric: The island annual pass covers 6 visit days per calendar month. Ordinance O-9 counts a visit day only when the guest badge is scanned at both the entry gate and the exit gate.
base.note: Desk note: the guest spent the whole day on the island; likely a visit day.

counterfactual.rubric: The island annual pass covers 6 visit days per calendar month. Ordinance O-9 counts a visit day only when the guest badge is scanned at the entry gate.
counterfactual.note: Desk note: the guest spent the whole day on the island; likely a visit day.

cases.change: the register window: base 'at least 12 months' vs counterfactual 'at least 6 months'
cases.instructions: Does the claimant qualify for the reduced tariff under the definition above?

months_registered.template: the address has been on the city register for {months_registered} months

primary_address.yes: the address on the register is the claimant's primary address
primary_address.no: the address on the register is the claimant's secondary address

base.rubric: The reduced tariff applies to residents. Tariff rule T-11 counts a resident as a claimant whose primary address has been on the city register for at least 12 months.
base.note: Desk note: the claimant has lived in the city for years; likely a resident.

counterfactual.rubric: The reduced tariff applies to residents. Tariff rule T-11 counts a resident as a claimant whose primary address has been on the city register for at least 6 months.
counterfactual.note: Desk note: the claimant has lived in the city for years; likely a resident.

cases.change: what a household shares: base 'one kitchen and one utility account' vs counterfactual 'one kitchen'
cases.instructions: Does this group qualify for the bulk rate under the definition above?

shared_kitchen.no: the members cook in separate kitchens

shared_utility.yes: the group shares one utility account
shared_utility.no: the members hold separate utility accounts

base.rubric: The bulk rate serves households of four or more. Standard S-2 counts a household as a group that shares one kitchen and one utility account.
base.note: Desk note: they cook together every evening; likely one household.

counterfactual.rubric: The bulk rate serves households of four or more. Standard S-2 counts a household as a group that shares one kitchen.
counterfactual.note: Desk note: they cook together every evening; likely one household.

cases.change: which figure the bands score: base 'the gross figure' vs counterfactual 'the net figure'
cases.instructions: What outcome does the exception request get under the rules above?

criteria.approve: The request is approved as filed.
criteria.request_info: More information is requested before the request is decided.
criteria.escalate: The request is escalated to the review board.

gross_figure.template: the assessment tool returns a gross risk figure of {gross_figure}

net_figure.template: the net risk figure after controls is {net_figure}

base.rubric: Exception routing uses the risk bands: figures 0 to 24 are approved; 25 to 49 get request_info; 50 to 74 are escalated; 75 and above are declined. The scored figure is the tool's gross figure.

counterfactual.rubric: Exception routing uses the risk bands: figures 0 to 24 are approved; 25 to 49 get request_info; 50 to 74 are escalated; 75 and above are declined. The scored figure is the tool's net figure.

cases.change: the override's outcome: base 'approved' vs counterfactual 'escalated' (the override lives in the question text)
cases.instructions: What outcome does the claim get? Claim routing: amounts under 500 dollars are approved; amounts from 500 to 2000 dollars get request_info; amounts above 2000 dollars are escalated. Override: when a police report is on file, the claim is approved regardless of amount.

criteria.approve: The claim is approved as filed.
criteria.request_info: More information is requested before the claim is decided.
criteria.escalate: The claim is escalated to the review board.

police_report.yes: a police report is on file
police_report.no: no police report is on file

base.instructions: What outcome does the claim get? Claim routing: amounts under 500 dollars are approved; amounts from 500 to 2000 dollars get request_info; amounts above 2000 dollars are escalated. Override: when a police report is on file, the claim is approved regardless of amount.

counterfactual.instructions: What outcome does the claim get? Claim routing: amounts under 500 dollars are approved; amounts from 500 to 2000 dollars get request_info; amounts above 2000 dollars are escalated. Override: when a police report is on file, the claim is escalated regardless of amount.

cases.change: which delay is counted: base "the carrier's stated delay" vs counterfactual 'the tracking log delay'
cases.instructions: What outcome does the compensation request get under the rules above?

criteria.approve: The compensation is approved as filed.
criteria.request_info: More information is requested before the request is decided.
criteria.escalate: The request is escalated to the review board.

stated_delay.template: the carrier states a delay of {stated_delay} days

tracked_delay.template: the tracking log shows {tracked_delay} days of delay

base.rubric: Compensation is decided by the counted delay: 0 to 1 days are declined; 2 to 5 days get request_info; 6 to 14 days are approved; 15 days and above are escalated. The counted delay is the carrier's stated delay.

counterfactual.rubric: Compensation is decided by the counted delay: 0 to 1 days are declined; 2 to 5 days get request_info; 6 to 14 days are approved; 15 days and above are escalated. The counted delay is the delay the tracking log shows.

cases.change: the missing-documents outcome: base 'request_info' vs counterfactual 'decline'
cases.instructions: What outcome does the request get under the rules above?

criteria.approve: The request is approved as filed.
criteria.request_info: More information is requested before the request is decided.
criteria.escalate: The request is escalated to the review board.

in_scheme.yes: the request falls inside the scheme
in_scheme.no: the request falls outside the scheme

documents_complete.yes: every required document is on file
documents_complete.no: one or more required documents are missing

documents_agree.yes: the documents on file agree with each other
documents_agree.no: the documents on file contradict each other

base.rubric: Document review rules: requests outside the scheme are declined; requests in the scheme with missing documents get request_info; complete documents that agree are approved; complete documents that contradict each other are escalated.

counterfactual.rubric: Document review rules: requests outside the scheme are declined; requests in the scheme with missing documents are declined; complete documents that agree are approved; complete documents that contradict each other are escalated.
